correctness.rationale: Exact densities follow from the primary 2026 class-count recurrence. Its generating functions obey a linear divisor recursion. A strong induction on divisors cancels the full Laurent principal part at the largest-prime singularity, using the sum-of-totients identity. Remaining poles have strictly larger modulus, yielding the exponentially precise tail by partial fractions. The packaged exact checker establishes 29 sample cancellations, 510 prime-power recurrence checks and 15 direct complete-period rational-orbit counts; no finite verification is mistaken for an unrestricted proof. Boundaries, the density-one input and fixed-denominator quantifiers are explicit.

value.rationale: The 2026 density-one theorem does not quantify the high-order tail for general composite denominators. This finding determines its sharp exponential constant, precise polynomial factor and leading coefficient uniformly across all lower-prime factors at each fixed denominator, and proves a stronger exact principal-part identity with an exponentially small correction. It answers a natural quantitative dynamical-number-theory question and provides a reusable structural lemma, without claiming to settle individual termination.
